events.text: Purchased commission as ensign in his father's regiment

events.text: Received or purchased lieutenant's commission in the 44th

evidence.quote: on May 2 , 1751 he received ( or purchased ) a lieutenants commission in the 44th

events.text: Sent with his regiment to North America for the French and Indian War

evidence.quote: He was sent with the regiment to North America in 1754

events.label: battle
events.text: Was with Braddock at the defeat at the Monongahela

evidence.quote: He was with Braddock at his defeat at the Battle of the Monongahela in 1755

events.text: Purchased captain's commission in the 44th for 900 pounds

evidence.quote: On June 11 , 1756 Lee purchased a Captains commission in the 44th

events.label: expedition
events.text: Took part in expedition against the French fortress of Louisbourg

evidence.quote: The following year he took part in an expedition against the French fortress of Louisbourg

events.label: wounded
events.text: Wounded in failed assault on Fort Ticonderoga

evidence.quote: on July 1 , 1758 he was wounded in a failed assault on Fort Ticonderoga

events.label: capture

evidence.quote: took part in the capture of Fort Niagara in 1759

events.label: capture
events.text: Took part in capture of Montreal

evidence.quote: took part in the capture of Fort Niagara in 1759 and Montreal in 1760

events.text: Returned to England after the Peace of Paris

evidence.quote: Lee returned to England in 1763 following the Peace of Paris

events.text: Served as aide-de-camp under King Stanislaus II

evidence.quote: In 1765 , Lee served as an aide-de-camp under King Stanislaus II

events.text: Returned to Poland after failing to win promotion in Britain

evidence.quote: in 1769 he returned to Poland

events.text: Promoted to lieutenant colonel while still inactive

evidence.quote: On 26 May 1772 , although still inactive , he was promoted to lieutenant colonel

events.text: Moved to North America and bought an estate in Virginia

evidence.quote: Lee moved to North America in 1773 and bought an estate in Virginia
He moved to the colonies in 1773

events.text: Volunteered to serve with rebel forces in the American War of Independence

evidence.quote: in 1775 , he volunteered to serve with rebel forces

events.text: Purchased estate worth 3,000 pounds in Berkeley County

evidence.quote: in 1775 purchased an estate worth £3,000 in Berkeley County

events.label: battle
events.text: Forces under his command repulsed British attempt to capture Charleston

evidence.quote: In 1776 , forces under his command repulsed a British attempt to capture Charleston

events.text: Named commander of the Canadian Department (never served in it)

evidence.quote: in 1776 , he was named commander of the so-called Canadian Department

events.text: Became second-in-command of the Continental Army when Ward resigned

evidence.quote: succeeded to second-in-command in 1776 when Ward resigned due to ill health

events.label: captured
events.text: Captured by British troops at Whites Tavern, Basking Ridge, New Jersey

evidence.quote: On December 12 , Lee was captured by British troops at Whites Tavern in Basking Ridge , New Jersey
Later that year , he was captured by British cavalry under Banastre Tarleton

events.label: manuscript
events.text: Wrote plan for British commissioners while a prisoner of war

evidence.quote: discovered a manuscript dated March 29 , 1777 , written by Lee while he was the guest of the British as a prisoner of war

events.label: released
events.text: Released on parole in a prisoner exchange

evidence.quote: Lee was released on parole as part of a prisoner exchange in early April 1778

events.text: Returned to duty as Washington's second-in-command

evidence.quote: returned to duty with the Continental Army as Washingtons second-in-command on May 21

events.label: war council
events.text: Argued at second war council against a major battle

evidence.quote: In June , as the British evacuated Philadelphia
At the second council , Lee argued the Continental Army was no match for the British Army

events.text: Took over command of the vanguard at Englishtown

evidence.quote: Lee took over on June 27 at Englishtown

events.label: battle
events.text: Battle of Monmouth: Lee's vanguard attack miscarried and forced a retreat

evidence.quote: When news arrived at 05:00 on June 28 that the British were moving , Lee led the vanguard towards Monmouth Court House
During the Battle of Monmouth later that year , Lee led an assault on the British that miscarried
Lee fought the counter-attacking British in a rearguard action that lasted no more than thirty minutes

events.label: confrontation
events.text: Washington confronted Lee over the disordered retreat at Monmouth

evidence.quote: When news arrived at 05:00 on June 28
Washington asked without pleasantries , I desire to know , sir , what is the reason

events.text: Relieved of command by Steuben at Englishtown

evidence.quote: When news arrived at 05:00 on June 28
At 15:00 , Steuben arrived at Englishtown and relieved Lee of command

events.label: letter
events.text: Sent insolent letter to Washington blaming him and demanding apology

evidence.quote: on June 30 , after protesting his innocence to all who would listen , Lee wrote an insolent letter to Washington

events.label: court-martial
events.text: Court-martial convened on three charges

evidence.quote: The court convened on July 4 , and three charges were laid before Lee

events.label: court-martial
events.text: Court-martial trial concluded

evidence.quote: The trial concluded on August 12

events.label: verdict
events.text: Found guilty on all three counts; verdict confirmed by Congress

evidence.quote: the verdict was confirmed by Congress on December 5

events.text: Letter to Congress led to termination of his army service

evidence.quote: In 1780 , Lee sent such a poorly received letter to Congress that it terminated his service with the army

events.label: death
events.text: Died of fever in a tavern in Philadelphia

evidence.quote: he was stricken with fever and died in a tavern on October 2 , 1782
